weather_line: Overcast with a low ceiling · household objects exactly where you did not put them

stories.headline: Third Object Placed; Configuration Is a Triangle; Lucy Has Been Pointing at the Biscuit Tin This Whole Time
stories.byline: By our domestic correspondent, filing from the kitchen doorway at a respectful distance
body: A third household object was discovered in precise placement early Thursday morning: the good wooden spoon, previously kept in the crock by the hob in a state of cheerful functional disorder, was found standing handle-down in the larder beside the oven mitt, equidistant from both the mitt and the biscuit tin. The three objects, when mapped by household analysts — working carefully and with chalk, treating the counter as a crime scene — form an isoceles triangle of exact proportion, with the biscuit tin at the apex.

Analysts have described the configuration as 'not random, not decorative, and not ambiguous.' The triangle points, by the most conservative geometric reading, directly at the biscuit tin. The biscuit tin, which has been at the apex of this arrangement for reasons that are now becoming clear, has not been opened. Its contents are believed to be intact. Lucy has not looked at it in four days.

A Ministry Household Dynamics consultant, reached by fire-call, said only: 'You are not the investigators in this situation. You have been the subjects.' He then rang off. Pemwick, still on secondment and technically without jurisdiction, asked if he could measure the triangle. He has been measuring the triangle. It is, he reports, extremely precise. No biscuit is missing. This, analysts now agree, is the most alarming part.

stories.headline: Thursday's Remaining Dispute Resolves Upon Hearing Christine's Name; Goblin Clerk Notes: 'That Is Also Precedent Now'
body: A long-standing dispute over a Gringotts sub-vault inheritance claim — a matter that had occupied four senior goblins, two ledgers of contradictory footnotes, and one frankly exhausted barrister since June — was resolved Thursday in a single pre-lunch session after Christine indicated she would be attending in person.

The relevant goblin, Klurk, reportedly reviewed his position overnight upon receiving her diary confirmation and arrived Thursday with revised documentation and a more cooperative expression than observers had previously believed his face capable of. The session lasted eleven minutes. The barrister wept briefly, from relief.

Gringotts' clerk of record has now noted the pattern formally: three consecutive disputes resolved upon the announcement of Christine's attendance, before her arrival, without her having yet said anything. The notation reads, 'C. — presence sufficient, remarks unnecessary.' This has been filed as precedent. Christine has been informed. She has described this as 'efficient.'

stories.headline: Pemwick's Triangle Measurements Submitted as Unsolicited Annex to the 'Wholesome, Not Misc.' Registry; Quoyne Has Not Yet Decided How He Feels About This
body: Junior analyst Pemwick, still formally unassigned following the closure of the Duck Bandit inquiry, submitted Thursday morning a fourteen-page unsolicited annex to the 'Wholesome, Not Misc.' Registry titled 'Geometric Evidence of Domestic Intent: A Preliminary Survey.' The annex contains seven diagrams, three tables of measurement, and a note at the end reading 'I believe the spoon is load-bearing.'

Registry Supervisor Quoyne received the annex at 9:14 a.m. and has been described by colleagues as 'reading it slowly' and 'making a face that could go either way.' The registry, which now contains two formal entries and a waiting list, was not designed to accommodate annexes. Quoyne has not rejected it. He has also not accepted it. He has placed it on the level shelf and stepped back.

Pemwick, asked whether he had been invited to contribute to the registry, confirmed that he had not. He has, however, measured the registry shelf. It is, he reports, level. He has noted this in the annex as Appendix B.

stories.headline: The Hollows Report Thursday as 'Still Waiting'; the Jeep Has Been Idling in Its Assessment; Steve Has Been Thinking About It Since Tuesday and Is Now Thinking About It Differently
stories.byline: By our Appalachian correspondent, perched on a ridgeline
body: Sources within the Appalachian enchanted highlands — specifically the fog-wrapped hollows below the main gorge, and the ridge Delphine Holt last walked in a northerly direction — have confirmed Thursday that conditions remain, quote, 'prime.' The rock arches have been described as patient. The mud has been described as 'invested.'

The Jeep, consulted via the usual method of standing near it and listening to what it does not quite say, has revised its position from 'ready' to 'expectant,' which experienced interpreters consider a meaningful escalation. Steve, who has been thinking about it since Tuesday, has been observed consulting maps. Then trail notes. Then the weather. Then the Jeep, briefly, and the Jeep did not discourage him.

Christine's assessment of the situation — logistical, precise, characteristically accurate — has not yet been formally issued. The hollows are, however, noted as 'aware she will have opinions and are factoring this in.' The mud, specifically, is said to be 'hoping.'

familiars_corner: Lucy: Has spent Thursday in a state of complete and unhurried calm — seated at the far end of the kitchen, tail curled, surveying the counter with the equanimity of someone whose plans are on schedule. She did not look at the spoon. She did not need to.

Ellie: Discovered the chalk triangle on the counter and found it very interesting. Sat inside it for approximately twelve minutes. Is not certain what it means but feels it was meant for her. Analysts have not commented on this. They did not want to make it worse.

Jersey: Has located the warmest corner of Thursday and is committed to it. The triangle, the spoon, the ongoing inquiry — all noted, all filed, all irrelevant. His lap situation is excellent and he intends to keep it that way.
founding_editor_note: If that triangle is load-bearing, you'll want to check the corners first — I'd have used quarter-round moulding. Just saying. — D.

in_brief.sport: Thursday's recreational lifting record stands; no formal challenge has been issued, and the barbell has been described as 'not expecting one.'
in_brief.forecast: Overcast through the afternoon, with a late clearing over the ridgelines; objects in the kitchen will continue to be exactly where you did not put them; the triangle holds.

storyline_updates.title: The Biscuit Tin Endgame
storyline_updates.summary: Day 3: A third object — the good wooden spoon — has been found placed equidistant from the oven mitt and the biscuit tin, forming a precise isoceles triangle with the tin at the apex. Pemwick has measured it and confirmed the geometry. The household now understands they are not the investigators; they are the subjects. No biscuit is missing. Day 4 (resolution): Lucy should complete her operation — either a biscuit disappears with zero trace and zero evidence at all (her masterwork), or the tin is found open and perfectly re-closed with no indication of how, and Lucy is discovered in an entirely different room, looking entirely elsewhere, having been there apparently all morning. The resolution should be funny, earned, and leave Lucy's guilt absolutely certain and absolutely unprovable. Pemwick files a final report. Quoyne reads it. The annex is accepted into the registry, reluctantly, because it is extremely precise.
